## Pushed — Gerrit change 2688. `make verify` GREEN.

**https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2688** — "Refuse force_new_store inside a
linked worktree", `Change-Id: Ie215f465cd252002db7b658a7722c956faf2ea7d`,
`rebar-ticket: 00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc`, DCO signed. Status NEW. **Not submitted.**

Vote state at push: `Code-Review`, `LLM-Review`, `Verified` all **no votes yet** (CI and the
review bot had not run).

### `make verify` — reported plainly, including the run that failed

**Run 1 FAILED (exit 2): 1 failed, 1 error, 19818 passed.** Both were caused by ONE line in
the file I added:

    FAILED tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py::test_no_tests_rooted_imports_anywhere_under_tests
    ERROR  tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_echo_loop_experiment.py — ImportError at collection

`test_echo_loop_experiment.py:30` used `from tests.integration.rebar_reconciler.test_reconcile_idempotency import …`
— a `tests.`-rooted absolute import. Neither `tests/__init__.py` nor
`tests/*/__init__.py` exists, so that resolves only with the **repository root** on
`sys.path`, which happens under `python -m pytest` (cwd insertion) and **dies at collection
under the bare `pytest` console script** — the project's canonical invocation, used by the
`Makefile` `test` target and `_build-and-test.yml`. This is the standing guard for bug `a371`.

**My targeted runs passed and the full suite did not, for exactly the reason that guard
documents.** I had been running the file directly, which put the rootdir on `sys.path`. This
is the case AGENTS.md makes for `make verify` not being optional, and it was worth the
57 minutes to find.

Fix: a bare sibling import, `from test_reconcile_idempotency import (…)` — the established
convention in that tree (e.g. `tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:18`).
Verified under **bare `pytest`** this time, not `python -m pytest`: 8 passed; the convention
guard passes; and `pytest -m "not integration and not external" --collect-only` collects
19899 / 20218 with **zero errors**.

**Run 2 PASSED (exit 0): 19827 passed, 80 skipped, 0 failures, 39m28s.** I re-ran the whole
contract rather than trusting a targeted re-check of a one-line change.

### `(bugfix-size-attestation)` — checked, and NOT required

Changes 2683 and 2684 each took `LLM-Review -1` on this criterion tonight, so I pre-empted it
using the gate's OWN counter rather than estimating:

    gate-computed non-test diff lines: 144
    threshold                       : 150
    -> UNDER the floor; no attestation required

`is_test_path` excludes only `tests/` and `conftest.py`, so `docs/release-notes.md` counts
toward the 144. `rebar review-plan --status` reports `unsigned` (free check, no LLM, no
network), which is fine at 144 lines.

**Margin is only 6 lines.** If review asks for a change adding more than 6 non-test lines,
the attestation becomes required — and the order then matters: description under the
8,000-char cap (currently 4,981), set/widen `file_impact` FIRST (currently 6 paths), then
run the review, because widening file impact afterwards stales the attestation just paid for.

### Discipline

No `--force` and no gate bypass on any rebar operation at any point. The one `caused_by` link
refused by its commit-evidence gate was resolved with the sanctioned `attach_commits` repair
path. Every process I started is reaped: 0 remaining under my worktree.
`scripts/check_orphaned_load.py` exits 1, but its single non-system finding is
`/Applications/Caffeine.app` — an operator desktop utility I did not spawn and did not kill.

### Still open, unchanged and not mine

AC6 (cleanup, running), AC7 (detector, blocked behind change 2683), AC8 (bridge re-enable).
The bridge stays disabled.
